text: A meditation for when something fires bigger than it should. Find a comfortable place to sit, somewhere you won't be disturbed for the next few minutes. Let your back be upright and not stiff. Let your hands rest easily on your lap, and whenever you're ready, Gently let your eyes closed— close. Let's begin with the breath. Not changing it, just noticing it. The air coming in, the air going out. And with each breath out, let your shoulders drop a little. Let the day loosen its grip. There's nowhere to go, nothing to fix, just this for a few minutes. Take one slow breath in through the nose, and a long slow breath out. And again, in, slowly out, letting yourself settle a little deeper. Now gently, I'd like you to bring to mind a small moment from your past when something bothered you more than it probably should have. Nothing huge, not your deepest wound, just a small one. Someone's tone, a message that stung, flash of irritation in traffic, or an anger with your family member. Let it come into focus. See it again. Hear it again. Just for a moment, let yourself feel the little edge of it. Now let's look at it gently in 3 layers. The first one is the body. Bring your attention down inside as you hold that moment. Is there a little heat in the chest, or buzzing in the whole body, tightness in the jaw, shoulders, Somewhere in the stomach. Just go looking softly. You don't have to change it, you don't have to make it go away, just notice it's there and quietly in your mind, Name it. This is a tightness in the chest. Now notice what your mind wants to say about that moment. They shouldn't have refused me. I'll get back to them. I'll tell them how wrong they were. I'll let— I'll not let them do this to me. How dare they! Just watch the story start up like a little engine turning over. You don't have to argue with it, you don't have to believe it, just see it for what it is— story. The mind is spinning, and gently name it. This is dash story. And now very gently see if you can feel the older thing underneath that story, the tender place it's pressing on, something quiet like, I don't matter, I'm not respected, I'm not enough. It might be faint, that's completely okay. You don't need to dig, just notice it's there, this old, soft, familiar ache, and name it kindly. This is dash dash dash, it's old belief. You just named all 3 of them, which means you are not them. You are the one who can see them. You are the one watching. Rest there for a moment as the one who watches, not fighting the feelings, not chasing the story, just watching it all with a little space around it now. Feel how from there, there's a room. The reaction may still be there, but it's all of you. You are the sky, you are— and it's just weather moving through you. Now take a slow breath in and let it go. And let it— small moment— dissolve. Let it drift off. You're done with it now. Gently begin to come back. Feel the seat beneath you. The ground under your feet, notice the sounds in the room around you. And when you're ready, in your own time, let your eyes open. You know the 3 names now: body, story, belief. Naming them is how you step back into the sky.
